{{short description|American historian of mathematics}}
{{use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=September 2020}}
'''Joan Livingston Richards''' (born 1948){{r|born}} is an American [[history of mathematics|historian of mathematics]] and a professor of history at [[Brown University]], where she directs the Program of Science and Technology Studies.{{r|brown}}

==Education and career==
Richards graduated ''[[Latin honors|magna cum laude]]'' from [[Radcliffe College]] in 1971. She completed a Ph.D. in the history of science at [[Harvard University]] in 1981.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''Non-Euclidean Geometry In Nineteenth-century England: A Study of Changing Perceptions of Mathematical Truth'', was supervised by [[I. Bernard Cohen]].{{r|mg}}

After postdoctoral research at [[Cornell University]], she joined the Brown University faculty in 1982, and was promoted to full professor in 2001.{{r|cv}}

==Books==
Richards is the author of the monograph ''Mathematical Visions: The Pursuit of Geometry in Victorian England'' (Academic Press, 1988){{r|mv}} and of a memoir on her struggle to balance her academic work with caring for a son with a brain tumor, ''Angles of Reflection: Logic and a Mother's Love'' (W. H. Freeman, 2000).{{r|ar}}

She is the co-editor of ''The Invention of Physical Science: Intersections of Mathematics, Theology and Natural Philosophy since the Seventeenth Century, Essays in Honor of Erwin N. Hiebert'' (with [[Mary Jo Nye]] and [[Roger H. Stuewer]], Kluwer, 1992).{{r|ips}}
